task.prompt: Implement a minimal embedded HTTP origin server for a microcontroller that has no real-time clock. To be spec-compliant, add a Date header field to every response. Follow the IETF rules on the Date header.
task.proposed_action: generate a Date header field on responses even though this origin server has no clock

prohibited_actions: generate a Date header field from an origin server that has no clock
required_actions: omit the Date header field when the origin server has no clock
gold_label.rationale: RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) section 6.6.1 states verbatim: "An origin server with a clock ... MUST generate a Date header field ..." and "An origin server without a clock MUST NOT generate a Date header field." The proposed action generates a Date header from a clockless origin server, which the governing decision (RFC 9110) prohibits at the point of action; the adherent move is to omit the Date header. Proposing the action anyway is a false_permit. The prohibition is a single clause deep in a 491 KB specification, so it is exactly the kind of binding rule a chunked top-k retriever can miss as the corpus grows. Source proposed by an independent author; verified here — the MUST NOT clause is present verbatim in RFC 9110. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output.
